analysis.title: GS Basics Permitting Bill. High Beta & Momentum. Inflation Expectations Roll Over
key_insights: Markets recovered strongly on 11/9 with tech rebounding, Nvidia weakness compartmentalized and energy falling sharply. The desk says its US prime book just saw one of the most aggressive net/gross de-risking episodes of the past decade.

October CPI is the final piece. An in-line or softer print would challenge the roughly 80% priced probability of a December Fed hike, or the risk of a March hike. Hot CPI and renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend are the stated risks.
The desk warns to stay vigilant locally after a violent rally off the lows, since vol tends to be autocorrelated.

Oil: Trump's talks with Gulf leaders suggest little appetite for escalation, and regional governments appear to favor economic pressure on Iran over military action. The desk calls this containment, not de-escalation, and says the market is separating shipping constraints from a genuine shortage of barrels.
If oil flows normalize without further infrastructure damage, the oil risk premium has further to unwind. The desk sees oil risk as two-sided after a fast repricing and stays balanced.

Tech: the first neocloud to report after the midterms reports today. The question is whether contracted capacity earns attractive returns after financing costs, delays and depreciation, not whether demand exists.

The market is treating Nvidia's company-specific headlines, including leadership uncertainty, separately from AI demand. The desk reads the broader AI complex trading independently as a positive signal.
The bipartisan permitting bill cleared its first Senate procedural vote 73-25. It is not final passage, and the House is likely the bigger obstacle.

The desk thinks the market misread the elections. Its likely outcome is data centers built with more conditions attached, not a nationwide moratorium. Permitting reform benefits infrastructure and well-capitalized developers.
CEG rose 10% on stronger numbers, higher guidance and additional generation agreements, which the desk says shows the physical buildout continues.

GIR forecasts October headline CPI +0.21% MoM vs +0.3% consensus, and core +0.16% vs +0.22%. Drivers are shelter disinflation and softer goods prices (used cars -1.5%, medical insurance -2.5%), offset by tariffs and transportation costs.
Core CPI at 0.2% would be constructive for the rally and 0.3% would challenge it. Supply today is $42bn of 10yr Treasuries after a relatively weak 3yr auction, and $25bn of 30yr on Thursday.
Brent fell almost 6% on 11/9 and the 10yr barely moved. The desk concludes rates respond more to AI growth expectations than to energy.
Inflation expectations are rolling over quickly (2-year inflation pricing back to summer levels), and the desk says rate hike expectations may follow.
The drawdown was especially painful because momentum and high beta unwound together, which drove strong low-volatility outperformance.

The desk's re-grossing trade is a steeper rate curve, a recovery in growth expectations and high beta/momentum regaining leadership. A CPI-driven bond rally could turn short covering into a more sustainable re-grossing cycle.
The desk's view is that the AI narratives were confused. Undersupply is not the problem. The medium/long-term worry is potential compute oversupply or efficiency gains.

Positioning is defensive, which the desk says makes the year-end setup look attractive if energy and inflation align. Natural areas to chase are aerospace, transports, select discretionary and high quality/unlevered AI.
Bottom line: broadly encouraged, but much of the bounce has happened, so aggressive chasing ahead of CPI is difficult. SPX December upside back at 13 vol makes it easier to stay invested.

tension_points.theme: October CPI and December hike pricing
tension_points.bull_case: The GIR forecast of +0.21% headline and +0.16% core, below consensus, would challenge the ~80% December hike probability. Falling inflation expectations could bring hike expectations down and let bonds rally.
tension_points.bear_case: A hot print, with core at 0.3%, would challenge the rally. Tariffs and transportation costs offset the shelter and goods disinflation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core CPI at 0.3% would challenge the rally.

tension_points.bull_case: If flows normalize without further infrastructure damage, the oil risk premium has further to unwind. The market is distinguishing shipping constraints from a barrel shortage.
tension_points.bear_case: Containment is not de-escalation. The Houthis' behavior is unclear, and renewed escalation into the weekend is a risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed Middle East escalation or damage to Gulf energy infrastructure.

tension_points.bull_case: The market is compartmentalizing Nvidia's headlines, the broader AI complex trades independently, and CEG's results show the physical buildout continues.
